subject: pharmacology
title: Selective Alpha-1 Blockers, Uroselective Antagonists, and Non-Selective Agents

steps.tx: The prototypic selective competitive alpha-1 adrenergic receptor antagonist is **prazosin**. By selectively blocking postjunctional vascular alpha-1 receptors with approximately one-thousand-fold higher affinity than presynaptic alpha-2 receptors, prazosin dilates both systemic resistance arterioles and capacitance veins without interrupting presynaptic auto-inhibitory feedback. Consequently, norepinephrine release is not augmented, and reflex tachycardia is significantly less prominent than with non-selective alpha antagonists.
steps.say: Prazosin selectively blocks alpha-1 receptors, dilating arterioles and veins with minimal reflex tachycardia.

vis.caption: Pharmacologic blockade of postjunctional vascular and prostatic alpha-1 adrenergic receptors.

steps.tx: Longer-acting structural congeners of prazosin sharing quinazoline cores include **terazosin and doxazosin**. Terazosin provides an elimination half-life of twelve hours, whereas doxazosin exhibits a prolonged half-life of twenty hours, allowing once-daily dosing in essential hypertension and benign prostatic hyperplasia. In addition to lowering vascular resistance, both agents relax prostatic smooth muscle and induce gradual apoptosis of prostatic stromal cells, improving peak urinary flow rates.
steps.say: Terazosin and doxazosin provide once-daily alpha-1 blockade, lowering blood pressure and improving urinary flow in BPH.

rows: Once daily in morning or bedtime

steps.tx: Targeted pharmacological relief of lower urinary tract symptoms without vascular hypotension is achieved with **tamsulosin**. As an uroselective antagonist, tamsulosin exhibits high selectivity for alpha-1A and alpha-1D adrenergic receptor subtypes localized in the prostate stroma, bladder neck, and proximal urethra, with negligible affinity for vascular alpha-1B receptors. It significantly enhances maximum urinary flow rates and relieves bladder outlet obstruction without altering systemic blood pressure.
steps.say: Tamsulosin selectively blocks alpha-1A prostatic receptors to improve urination without causing hypotension.

vis.alt: Normal prostate versus benign prostatic hyperplasia
vis.caption: Anatomical compression of the prostatic urethra in benign prostatic hyperplasia targeted by uroselective alpha-1A antagonists.

steps.tx: An ultra-selective alpha-1A receptor antagonist offering the highest ratio of prostatic to vascular selectivity is **silodosin**. Possessing thirty-fold greater affinity for alpha-1A over alpha-1B receptors, silodosin produces rapid clinical improvement in American Urological Association symptom scores in men with benign prostatic hyperplasia. Because alpha-1A receptors also govern smooth muscle contraction in the vas deferens and seminal vesicles, retrograde ejaculation is the most common side effect.
steps.say: Silodosin offers extreme alpha-1A selectivity for bladder outlet symptoms, frequently causing retrograde ejaculation.

left.title: Silodosin (Alpha-1A ultra-selective)
points: Minimal risk of systemic orthostatic hypotension
Rapid onset of urinary flow improvement

right.title: Prazosin (Alpha-1 non-selective)
points: Requires dosage titration to avoid syncope

steps.tx: The historic irreversible, non-competitive alpha-adrenergic antagonist is **phenoxybenzamine**. As a haloalkylamine derivative, phenoxybenzamine undergoes spontaneous cyclization in body fluids to form a reactive ethyleniminium intermediate that forms a permanent covalent bond with alpha-1 and alpha-2 adrenergic receptors. Recovery of tissue responsiveness requires de novo synthesis of fresh receptor proteins over three to four days, making it the definitive preoperative agent in pheochromocytoma.
steps.say: Phenoxybenzamine covalently binds alpha receptors, providing irreversible blockade essential before pheochromocytoma surgery.

nodes.label: Spontaneous intramolecular cyclization to ethyleniminium ion
Covalent alkylation of alpha-1 and alpha-2 receptor binding sites
Irreversible blockade: Recovery requires new receptor protein synthesis

steps.tx: A rapid-acting, reversible competitive non-selective alpha-1 and alpha-2 antagonist is **phentolamine**. Administered intravenously, phentolamine blocks vascular alpha-1 receptors to relieve acute hypertensive crises precipitated by clonidine withdrawal, MAO inhibitor-tyramine interactions, or intraoperative catecholamine surges during pheochromocytoma manipulation. Concurrently blocking presynaptic alpha-2 receptors enhances norepinephrine release, producing prominent reflex tachycardia and cardiac arrhythmias that limit its long-term outpatient utility.
steps.say: Phentolamine reversibly blocks alpha-1 and alpha-2 receptors to rescue acute hypertensive crises.

right.title: Phenoxybenzamine (Irreversible covalent)
points: Overcomes surge spikes during tumor resection

steps.tx: A selective competitive alpha-2 adrenergic receptor antagonist historically investigated for erectile dysfunction is **yohimbine**. Extracted from the bark of Pausinystalia yohimbe, yohimbine blocks presynaptic inhibitory alpha-2 autoreceptors in the brainstem and peripheral sympathetic endings. This enhances central sympathetic outflow, increases norepinephrine release, elevates blood pressure and heart rate, and promotes penile cavernosal engorgement while inducing prominent central anxiety and tremors.
steps.say: Yohimbine selectively blocks alpha-2 receptors, boosting sympathetic outflow and norepinephrine release.

steps.tx: An intraoperative surgical complication uniquely associated with systemic alpha-1A antagonist exposure is **intraoperative floppy iris syndrome**. In patients taking tamsulosin or silodosin, prolonged blockade of iris dilator smooth muscle alpha-1A receptors causes permanent muscular flaccidity and pupillary constriction. During cataract phacoemulsification, the iris flutters billowingly, prolapses into corneal incisions, and constricts progressively, substantially elevating risks of posterior lens capsule rupture and vitreous loss.
steps.say: Tamsulosin causes intraoperative floppy iris syndrome, complicating cataract surgery with iris prolapse.
